page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5g.8xlarge is a storage-oriented instance belonging to the Local SSDs instance family. Built on the KVM hypervisor, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor based on the x86_64 architecture running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system provides 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type.

A defining feature of this configuration is its integrated 1919 GB local SSD storage, which delivers low-latency I/O performance directly connected to the host hardware. For external communication and cluster integration, the instance delivers a baseline network throughput of 16 Gbps. The provision of zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses indicates that deployments typically reside within private Virtual Private Cloud network architectures, leveraging internal routing or network gateways.

The combination of dedicated Intel Xeon cores, a balanced CPU-to-memory ratio, and direct-attached solid-state storage makes ecs.i5g.8xlarge effective for I/O-intensive workloads. Common deployments include relational databases, NoSQL engines, distributed caching systems, search indexes, and log analysis pipelines. While the local SSD provides rapid read and write access, it requires operational strategies for data persistence and node redundancy across clusters.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5g.8xlarge is an instance from the Local SSDs family designed for storage-centric and data-intensive tasks. Powered by the KVM hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor on x86_64 architecture, it offers 32 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system RAM, providing an even 4.0 GB allocation per core, along with 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present. Direct storage needs are addressed via a bundled 1919 GB local SSD volume, providing rapid local data access without reliance on network-attached disks. This configuration delivers an efficient resource balance for input/output intensive scenarios where local read and write operations are critical. Primary workloads include high-throughput databases, NoSQL data stores, search indexing engines, distributed caching layers, and high-performance analytical processing.
